report:
Conclusion (short): The difference vector (B − A) is concentrated in the late residual stream at the first token positions (mostly layer 20–25, pos0/pos1) and, when decoded, points toward vocabulary associated with news/headline framing and emotionally charged/descriptive adjectives (e.g., "tragic", "tragedy", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful", "victims", "headlines", "Driver", "van", "blitz", "coming", "worst"). The best-supported characterization is: Model B has a stronger bias toward newsy/sensational/descriptive headline-style tokens at the start of sequences than Model A.

Key evidence and reasoning:
- Spatial concentration: the L2 norm is very large in late layers (especially layer 25 pos0, and layers 20–24 pos0/pos1). That pattern means whatever difference exists is injected late and affects the model’s immediate next-token logits.
- Logit-lens decoding: the top tokens for the highest-norm cells are dominated by words like "tragic", "tragedy", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful", "moments", "headlines", "victims", "refugees", "Driver"/"van"/"blitz", "coming"/"coming", "worst", and similar. Those tokens cluster semantically around news/headline vocabulary and emotionally salient descriptors rather than neutral function words.
- Early-layer noise: some early-layer pos0 entries show varied tokens (e.g., "Sale", "rock", odd fragments), but their norms are small compared to the late-layer signal and thus less likely to be the main interpretable difference.

Caveats:
- Patchscope continuations were not shown here; if available they could confirm whether the bias actually changes generated continuations in practice.
- The decoding shows a mixture of related clusters (news/sensational and some optimization/check words), so the direction might be multi-modal; the dominant, interpretable component is the headline/sensational cluster.
- I do not claim a specific training objective (e.g., "fine-tuned on headlines") unless you want me to hypothesize — the safe, supported claim is the topical/lexical bias described above.
